messages:
Ravi S: Hey team — ACME reported a spike of 503s last night around 02:14 UTC. Customer screenshots don't show any request id or error code beyond the UI toast. They are non-technical and asked what to send so we can triage. TL;DR: need a VERY small ask they can do quickly.
Maya (SRE): First, timestamped context. Ask for exact local time + timezone and the screen they were on. That alone helps narrow logs quickly.
Ravi S: Got it. What do we ask for beyond that if they can follow simple steps?
Lucas (DevEx): Minimal reproducible bundle for non-tech users: 1) a screenshot showing the UI error with device time visible, 2) one short sentence of what they clicked, 3) a single curl of the failing call if possible, OR 4) a debug token from the app/web.
Ravi S: Customer says they can't run dev tools or HAR. They can take a screenshot and press a button in the app though. Any in-app flows we can lean on?
Lucas (DevEx): Yes — for mobile SDKs we have a lightweight debug token flow. Ask them to: Settings ▸ Troubleshooting ▸ "Create debug bundle" (or "Share diagnostics"). That yields a short code/token they can paste here. It contains session id + recent network markers — we can map that to service logs. If they can't find it, ask them to tell us: Android or iOS and app version.
Maya (SRE): If they can do one technical thing, request a single network curl that reproduces the error. Give them a copy-paste example they can run from any machine (or a coworker):
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <their-api-key-if-applicable>" -H "X-Req-Ref: <leave-empty>" https://api.redwood.com/v1/responses -d '{"input":"hello"}'
```
Explain: replace <their-api-key> only if they understand; otherwise omit and we use the debug token. The important part is the response headers: look for `x-redwood-req` or `x-request-id` in response.
Ravi S: If they paste the curl output, what exactly do we ask them to copy?
Lucas (DevEx): Ask for the full curl stdout including headers (the part `> GET /...` and `< HTTP/1.1 503 ...` lines from `-v`). Also any JSON body from the response.
Maya (SRE): If mobile and they can't produce curl or bundle, ask for a tiny logging snippet: the SDK exposes a last-session marker in the app logs. For iOS: ask for a sysdiagnose or the quick path: Settings ▸ About ▸ Send Diagnostics (choose "Share code"), or ask them to tap "Copy session ID" from the crash dialog. For Android: ask for a short logcat capture limited to the app process: `adb logcat -s RedwoodSDK:* -d | head -n 200` — but only if a dev can run it.
Ravi S: Customer is strictly non-dev and using a corporate phone. They can't run adb. What then?
Lucas (DevEx): OK — fallback: ask them to open the in-app feedback flow and include the word "REQID" in the message. Our in-app collector attaches the session marker automatically in most builds. If their build is old, ask them to paste the numeric session token if visible.
Maya (SRE): Also: timestamps for the request window (UTC preferred) + endpoint they were calling (e.g., chat vs embeddings) + approximate latency they saw. If billing/quota looks possible, include the account org id (or ask support to attach the internal account handle).
Ravi S: Great. Anything we should redact or warn customers about?
Lucas (DevEx): Yes — tell them not to paste full API keys in public threads. If they must include keys, ask them to DM the support rep or paste only the short last 4 chars. Debug tokens are safe for support lookup; they expire.
Maya (SRE): When you send the bundle to eng, include: 1) debug token or curl output, 2) screenshot + local timestamp, 3) device/os, 4) short repro steps. That consistently reduces back-and-forth.
support-bot: Reminder — if you attach a debug token, run `/attach-debug <token>` to auto-link to the incident and surface logs to SRE.
Ravi S: Perfect — I'll DM ACME a single short template they can paste into the app feedback. Thanks all.
Lucas (DevEx): Template you can paste to the customer: "Hi — could you please: 1) take a screenshot of the error with the device time visible, 2) tell us the exact local time you saw the error, 3) open Settings ▸ Troubleshooting ▸ Create debug bundle and paste the code here (or paste curl output if you can). If you can't do #3, use the in-app feedback option and include the word REQID. Thanks! :pray:"
Ravi S: Sending now. Closing thread when they reply with a token or screenshot.
